name: Steve — out of practice, and already told
summary: Around 80 hours built up over years, but a bad run: a house move, a new job, and nothing flown in three months. Only ten hours in the last year. His coach has told him to get current before changing wings. He gets tense when it's rough and wants to land, and he's starting to think a better wing might help.
why_this_persona: The currency case, and the multi-gate case. Two gates fire from completely different directions — currency and direct instructor advice — and gates short-circuit, so no threshold rule may be reported. Also tests that 'want_more_performance' is not what caused the Not yet.

notes: Computed skills 53.6, psychological 67.0, total 60.0, no bonus. The total is in the Nearly ready band, which is exactly why the gates matter: without them he would be told 'nearly'.

Both gates must fire and be reported. 'no_recent_flying' is the one currency gate the evidence supports at this step, because the only boundary-specific figures anywhere are annual-hours figures. 'instructor_said_wait' fires independently.

Gates short-circuit, so 'rules_expected' must be empty. He would otherwise also trip critical_check_floor (active_piloting at 0.45) and arguably the skills floor, but the engine must not report either. gate_behaviour.evaluation_order in config/scoring/low-b-to-mid-b.json requires this.

Negative check on knowledge/disagreements.md point 9: his motive is 'want_more_performance', which scores 0.8 and is not the reason for the result. A reviewer reading his output should see currency and his coach's advice, nothing about his reasons for wanting the wing.

'get_eyes_on_your_flying' must NOT fire: someone qualified has already watched him and given an answer, so suggesting he find someone would be absurd. 'test_fly_first' must not fire either — it is gated to ready/nearly_ready results.

'post_collapse_support' must not fire. He has never had a collapse and reports no incidents; his tense response to rough air is handled by 'nerves_are_not_the_problem' instead, which is about building the habit rather than recovering from an event.
